question: Should Android support device control, ADB-style access, and dynamic program execution as built-in node commands, a generic node/plugin tool surface, or not at this time?
rationale: The remaining work changes phone authority and remote execution boundaries, and repository policy requires maintainer intent before adding this kind of high-power capability.

options.title: Design explicit safe Android commands
options.body: Approve a narrow design for specific device controls first, with per-command permissions, gateway allowlist behavior, docs, tests, and real Android proof before any ADB or dynamic execution work.

options.title: Route through node-hosted tools
options.body: Wait for the generic node-hosted tool/API direction and let Android expose high-power tools only through that approved extension boundary.

options.title: Decline dynamic execution for now
options.body: Keep existing Android data and media commands but reject ADB and arbitrary Kotlin/script execution until a stronger sandbox and operator model exists.

recommendation.title: Design explicit safe Android commands
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow design for specific device controls first, with per-command permissions, gateway allowlist behavior, docs, tests, and real Android proof before any ADB or dynamic execution work.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Android node contract work makes this the best available routing signal for the security and command-surface decision.
